- opened 2026-08-26 (P06 NAGA build lane, slice 1; found while grounding the migration that RULING B1 made necessary — **DEFECT DESCRIPTION CORRECTED 2026-08-26 by a cross-family refuter, in a follow-up PR because the queue had already frozen the original; the conclusion stands, the named mechanism was unreachable**) | **Research OS valid-time is not text-orderable, so the bitemporal query P06 needs cannot be indexed at all today — the WRONG index builds fine and the RIGHT one is refused by PostgreSQL** | **THE CORRECTION FIRST, because this row shipped naming a mechanism nothing can reach.** It claimed `UtcDateTime` (`packages/research-os-core/research_os/primitives.py:362`) "does NOT canonicalise the serialised text", with `2026-01-15T00:00:00Z` / `...+00:00` / `...00.000Z` as three strings for one instant. **That is FALSE for the sanctioned write path**: `model_dump(mode="json")` collapses all three to `...T00:00:00Z` — re-measured 2026-08-26 in the repo venv. A mutation test could not have caught it; the tests were internally consistent and simply pinned something unreachable. **The conclusion survives through a stronger mechanism that requires no misbehaviour at all: the canonical form's fractional part is OPTIONAL.** At microsecond zero it is omitted entirely (`...T00:00:00Z`); otherwise it is emitted at full width (`...T00:00:00.500000Z`). `.` is 0x2E and `Z` is 0x5A, so inside a single second the instant at microsecond zero is chronologically FIRST and lexicographically LAST. Measured against live PostgreSQL 127.0.0.1:5432 this turn, not argued, on two instants written by the SAME compliant serialiser: `$1::text::timestamptz < $2::text::timestamptz` is TRUE while `$1::text < $2::text` is FALSE, and a half-open `valid_from <= T` predicate over `payload->'time'->>'valid_from'` SILENTLY DROPS a row that is inside the interval by the clock — exactly the class `fixtures/bitemporal/*` exist to catch. **The three-spelling hazard remains real but is scoped differently, and not merely to a misbehaving writer**: `_UTC_OFFSET_PATTERN = r"(?:Z|\+00:00)$"` (`primitives.py:84`) lives inside a `WithJsonSchema` block — it documents the PUBLISHED JSON Schema rather than validating input, it explicitly permits BOTH terminators, and it says nothing whatsoever about sub-second width. An independent producer building against that published schema is entitled to both spellings and to any fraction; pydantic narrows the terminator by accident of its default serialiser, and nothing narrows the width. **LATENCY, measured: there are ZERO production writers of `research_os_objects` in the tree** — the only `INSERT INTO research_os_objects` in EXECUTABLE code is inside migration 280's own test — so no CODE PATH IN THIS REPOSITORY can produce a mis-ordered row. **Stated precisely because a second cross-family door (Kimi K3) caught the loose version and it was verified true**: four further occurrences of that exact string DO exist in the tree, as text inside `evidence/2026-08/agent-nuzantara-backend-rag-ros-v1-p04-d2-contra-0e9fe85c/pack.yml:84,93,100` and `...-d5-trunca-cb8a4fa4/pack.yml:33` — the last an executed `cmd:` against a throwaway docker Postgres. They are records of what was done, not code paths that run, so the substance held while the sentence did not. Scoped deliberately: this is a measurement of the tree, NOT of a live database — it does not exclude an external producer or a manual insert, and no live count was taken. This is a defect waiting at the entrance of the lane that writes the first row, which is when it is cheapest to fix. The correct expression cannot be indexed either: `text::timestamptz` resolves through `timestamptz_in`, which `pg_proc.provolatile` reports as STABLE (`s`), and an index expression must be IMMUTABLE — PostgreSQL refuses the CREATE INDEX outright (asserted by attempting it, not only by reading the catalogue). The asymmetry is the danger: the wrong index is perfectly legal and looks healthy. Storage context, measured: migration 279 keeps the whole canonical object in one `payload JSONB` and its GIN `jsonb_path_ops` index serves containment (`@>`) lookups — `claim_family_id`, `status`, `review.state` are all already served; system-time is served by the existing `(object_kind, recorded_at DESC)` B-tree. **Valid-time range is the ONLY unserved shape, and it is unservable.** | missing arming step: decide, on Work Packet 04's surface, how a canonical instant is represented for ORDERING. Two coherent answers, neither taken here — **and the correction NARROWS (a) considerably: pydantic already emits the single `Z` spelling, so the only missing half is pinning the sub-second WIDTH** — (a) fix the wire form on write (always emit `.ffffff`, or always truncate to whole seconds) so lexicographic order IS chronological order and a plain text expression index becomes correct, which also makes `object_hash` stable across re-serialisation, and tighten `_UTC_OFFSET_PATTERN` so the PUBLISHED schema stops granting what the implementation does not; or (b) give the substrate an IMMUTABLE-safe normalised representation (a generated/stored column, or an IMMUTABLE parse helper) so the timestamptz expression becomes indexable. (a) is cheaper, fixes hashing too, and is now a smaller change than this row originally implied; (b) leaves the wire form free. Do NOT resolve it by adding a CHECK constraint from a domain packet: migration 279's own table comment says "Work Packet 04 owns this table; domain packets build adapters/projections on top, never a parallel core". | owner: me (the lane that owns Work Packet 04's contract surface — NOT the P06 build lane, which found it and is deliberately not deciding it) | proof-of-armed: `apps/backend-rag/backend/tests/db/test_research_os_valid_time_is_not_text_orderable.py` (8 tests) pins the facts and is DELIBERATELY a test of the current limitation — when the limitation is lifted, **4 of its 8 tests go red for a canonical-serialisation cure** and must be deleted in the same change that lifts it. A red there is the arming signal, not a regression. **SECOND CORRECTION, same day, and it is the one that makes this row's proof real.** The first correction proved the new mechanism against a LOCAL STAND-IN — a bare `BaseModel` carrying one `UtcDateTime` field — and called it "the real serialiser". A cross-family refuter simulated the actual cure where a cure would actually land (a serialiser on the canonical model layer) and showed the real writer switching to fixed precision **while every synchronous test in the module stayed GREEN**: the promise held only for a cure that happened to touch the stand-in, which is `lesson_a_cure_can_land_on_the_heir_and_leave_the_source_lying` inverted — the TEST landed on the heir. The same refuter also caught that the schema test was a TAUTOLOGY (it asserted ASCII relations among three hardcoded literals and never validated against the published schema, so it would have stayed green if `_UTC_OFFSET_PATTERN` were deleted) and that the PostgreSQL test OVERSOLD (it compared text parameters that never reached a payload, proving how PostgreSQL compares two strings — not that a stored object comes back out of order). All three are fixed: every value now derives from the REAL `ClaimTime`/`ValidTime`; the schema test runs `jsonschema.validate` against `ClaimTime.model_json_schema()` with a guilt control (`+0000` must be REFUSED, or the innocence loop would pass against a schema constraining nothing); and the PostgreSQL test INSERTs three real JSONB rows out of insertion order and asserts the real `ORDER BY payload->'time'->>'valid_from'` returns the EARLIEST row LAST, plus that the half-open predicate admits 1 of the 2 rows the clock puts inside. **Mutation-checked 2026-08-26 with bytecode disabled (`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` + `python -B`, compiled from text — W121), by applying THE CURE AT THE REAL MODEL LAYER** — a `PlainSerializer` with fixed sub-second width added to `UtcDateTime` in `primitives.py` itself, then reverted and verified clean: **4 valid reds** including the end-to-end PostgreSQL one, where the pre-correction module scored **0 red for the identical cure** — that DELTA is the proof, not the absolute count. A cross-family round-2 refuter then caught that a 5th red was COLLATERAL and not a signal: `test_the_compliant_write_path_canonicalises_the_three_spellings` asserted the collapsed value equals the literal `2026-01-15T00:00:00Z`, so a fixed-width cure failed it for the wrong reason — canonicalisation still worked, only the hardcoded expectation was coupled to the old representation. Fixed: it now asserts the three spellings collapse to ONE value, whatever that value is. **And the promise is NARROWED to what it can actually deliver**, which is the round-2 refuter's decisive point: these tests go red for a cure applied to CANONICAL SERIALISATION, and they CANNOT go red for cure (b) below — a substrate-level normalised/generated column or IMMUTABLE helper lifts the limitation by routing AROUND the text expression, leaving every assertion here correctly green. Nor do they observe a cure applied at the storage/adapter boundary, on the outer `Claim` model, or to `valid_to` (never exercised). Whoever arms this row must therefore treat a GREEN suite as compatible with the limitation having been lifted by (b), and confirm the arming from the migration/adapter that lifts it — not from this module alone. The 3 that stay green are correct to stay green — the published-schema hole and the two index facts are untouched by a serialiser cure. **Version skew closed by measurement, not by reasoning**: local Postgres is 17.8 but CI runs `public.ecr.aws/docker/library/postgres:15` (`tests.yml:773-789`), and both catalogue assertions here are version-sensitive by nature (`pg_proc.provolatile`, and the exact wording of the refused-index error). Re-run against a real **PostgreSQL 15.19** container: green. **CI reach verified too** — `backend/tests/db/` is inside `shard_tests.py::DEFAULT_TARGETS` and excluded only for `backend/tests/e2e`, there is NO `-m "not integration"` deselection anywhere in the backend-rag invocation, the `integration` marker is registered in both `pytest.ini:53` and `pyproject.toml:277-280` (so `--strict-markers` does not trip), and the same job wires `TEST_DATABASE_URL` at the Postgres service. Scoped deliberately: that is CONFIGURATION evidence that the file is routed and a database is available — it is not a receipt from a specific run, and none is claimed.

- opened 2026-08-26 (GARUDA VOA L7 CRM-handoff lane, M5) | **A GARUDA practice created in the CRM by the new L7 adapter carries NO SLA date: `OrderSnapshot.submit_by_date` is hardcoded `None`, so the operations team receives a practice with a price and a case type and no internal deadline to work to.** Found while building the concrete `OrderSnapshotProvider` (PR #5020) and deliberately left uncured rather than papered over. The adapter reads the new results table `garuda_voa_check_results` (migration 286), and that table **does not have a `submit_by_date` column at all** — verified against the live schema, 21 columns, no such field; only the LEGACY `garuda_voa_checks` table (the L2 table this order flow does not write) carries one. The value is produced by the engine as `VoaVerdict.submit_by_date` (`garuda_flow/intake.py:157`) and simply not persisted by 286. **Why it is `None` and not derived**: the row DOES carry `published_filing_deadline`, and mapping one onto the other is the obvious-looking move — but they are different dates by construction. `published_filing_deadline` is the customer-facing D-7 checkpoint (the only date this product is allowed to show publicly); `submit_by_date` is the INTERNAL operating-calendar commitment computed by `build_verdict` against `operating_calendar.last_open_day_before`. Asserting an equivalence nobody has verified is exactly how a plausible invention becomes a downstream fact, so the adapter returns `None` and `test_submit_by_date_is_none_and_not_the_published_deadline` pins that it keeps doing so. **Not yet customer-visible**: nothing constructs the adapter, so no CRM practice has been created by this path — the debt is real but currently latent, and it becomes operational the moment the handoff is armed. Cheap to get wrong quietly: a future reader sees an unused `published_filing_deadline` two lines away from a `None` and "fixes" it | missing arming step: decide WHERE the internal commitment comes from and wire it — either (a) persist `submit_by_date` on `garuda_voa_check_results` at check time (a migration plus a writer change in L2's check store, making the adapter a straight field copy like every other), or (b) recompute it in the adapter from the engine's own function rather than from the published deadline, which keeps the two dates independent but puts a second copy of the rule outside `build_verdict`. (a) is the smaller lie; (b) is faster and duplicates a rule. This is a design call, not a typo, which is why it is a row and not a follow-up commit | me (GARUDA VOA L7 lane, sessione M5 — own PR from fresh origin/main, NOT folded into #5020 which is armed) | proof-of-armed: a practice created end-to-end by the armed handoff carries a `submit_by_date` that MATCHES what `intake.build_verdict` returns for the same case — compared against the engine's own output, never against `published_filing_deadline` — and a guilt check: a case whose D-7 checkpoint and internal commitment fall on DIFFERENT days (one where `last_open_day_before` actually moves the date) shows the two as different, proving the field is not silently the published date wearing another name

- opened 2026-08-02 | **`merge=union` on this ledger makes GitHub call EVERY ledger-touching PR conflicted, while every git client merges it cleanly — and the documented escape fails too** | `.gitattributes` on main declares `.claude/skills/modus/PENDING-ARMS.md merge=union`, a BUILT-IN git driver that resolves by keeping both sides' lines — exactly right for an append-only registry, and the reason no session has ever hand-resolved this file. But GitHub's mergeability computation does **not** apply `.gitattributes` merge drivers: it runs a plain three-way merge and reports `mergeable: false` / `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`. Measured on PR #3527 with both sides looking at the SAME base (`04b3eb38e`) and the SAME head (`aa7d97029`): GitHub said `dirty`, `git merge --no-commit` succeeded cleanly in BOTH directions, and `gh pr update-branch` — the documented server-side fix — failed with "Cannot update PR branch due to conflicts". The only path is a LOCAL merge of main into the branch, then a push (on M5 that costs a full pre-push suite). The danger is not the delay: a session reading `mergeable: false` as a real conflict will either burn a cycle hunting a conflict that does not exist, or — far worse — hand-edit the ledger to "resolve" it and drop the other side's lines, which is precisely the loss `merge=union` was added to prevent. Verified on this merge that the driver does its job: 269 open rows on the branch + 265 on main -> **270** after, nothing lost, `phantom_operator=0 malformed=0`. - opened 2026-08-01 | **CodeQL findings cannot block a merge in this repo, and the obvious way to make them block BREAKS THE MERGE QUEUE — measured, by breaking it** | The two required contexts `CodeQL Analysis (python|javascript)` are matrix JOB completions: they go green whatever the scan found, so they prove the scanner RAN, never that it found nothing. Earlier this session I promoted the aggregate `CodeQL` context to required (26 -> 27) to close that. **It hung the entire merge queue.** #3496 sat at position 1 in `AWAITING_CHECKS` for ~50 minutes with 38/38 checks green on the queue ref and exactly one required context missing — `CodeQL` — with a sibling lane's #3460 stacked behind it, and every PR opened afterwards would have hit the same wall. Cause, verified rather than guessed: that check is posted by the GitHub **code-scanning app** (`app.id 57789`) when it processes the SARIF **for a pull request**; a merge-queue ref is not a PR, so it is never posted there — the requirement is unsatisfiable by construction, not flaky. `security.yml` already declares `merge_group:` and its matrix jobs DO report on the queue ref, which is exactly what made the gap invisible. Reverted to 26 contexts and confirmed server-side; the queue drained to 0 within minutes. **The lesson is mine and is the one I keep writing**: I ran a positive control before arming it — "does code scanning attribute alerts to a pull ref?" — and answered it only on the PR path, never on the merge_group path. That is not style, it is **W69** — a required check that is path-skipped never reports and leaves the PR pending forever, named in-repo by `asyncpg-lint.yml:10`, `actionlint.yml:14`, `adversarial-review-gate.yml:12`, `npm-lock-sync.yml:28`, `p3-sandbox-gates.yml:20`, `hook-innocence-gate.yml:24`, `guard-conformance.yml:12`. `wr3-spend-gate-tests.yml` carries `paths:` on BOTH `pull_request` and `push`, so promoting it as it stands would pend-forever every PR in the repo that touches no WR3 path. A path-scoped middle road exists only with a skip→success sentinel job (`catD-backend-data-invariants.yml:38` names it); nothing in this repo implements one, so building it is its own packet, not a step here. Recommendation on file: **(B)** — this guards a credit-spend breaker and the repo already treats cost breakers as required — but it changes branch protection for the whole fleet, so it waits for a quiet queue and is declared before it is done, never slipped in. - closed 2026-08-22 (m5, ops/spalla-hook-secret-leak lane) | **The deferred backslash-escaped-quote class is cured IN the same PR that deferred it — half as a side effect of the architecture change, half by an explicit anchor fix, and the two halves turned out to be DIFFERENT diseases** | The row opened earlier today asked for its own diff, on the grounds that touching rule 2 core plus every rule ASSIGN_TAIL was the blast radius that had already produced three leak directions. That reasoning expired when the cascade architecture was deleted: there is no ASSIGN_TAIL and no rule ORDER left to disturb. What the deferral got RIGHT, and what is worth carrying forward, is that the class was not one thing. (a) TAIL CONTAINMENT — `TOKEN="abc\" <v>"`, where VALUE quoted branches stop at the escaped quote — died with the cascade, because VALUE no longer has to find where a value ENDS, only that an assignment BEGINS; measured, not assumed. (b) ANCHOR RECALL — `curl -d "{\"api_key\": \"<v>\"}"`, the ordinary way to write a JSON body inside a double-quoted shell arg — did NOT die with it and had to be fixed on purpose: the separator is preceded by a backslash-escaped quote, so no anchor matched at all and the line was logged unchanged BYTE FOR BYTE. A cut that runs to end-of-string is no defence where nothing anchors. That distinction is the durable lesson: soundness of the CUT and recall of the ANCHOR are separate obligations, and proving the first says nothing about the second. | proof: 12 new guilt cases (5 tail-containment, 4 backslash, 3 anchor-recall) FAIL on the pre-change hook and nothing else does (12/117), all 117 pass after (100 guilt / 15 innocence / 2 mode), shellcheck clean, guard-conformance 0 violations. - closed 2026-07-24 | NEW SCAR (candidate W103, family #9 State-schema mutation drift — a proxy lied about state) — PR #2961 spent ~6 rounds (~1.5h wall-clock) of merge-origin/main→regen-docs→prettier→push, with `gh pr view 2961` persistently reporting `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`/`mergeable: CONFLICTING` after every single push, despite the diff visibly resolving each time. Root cause: the local/worktree branch had silently drifted in NAME from the PR's actual tracked branch — pushes were landing on `agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines-repair`, a branch with no PR at all, while PR #2961 tracks `agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines` (no `-repair` suffix), whose head (`5d8eeadc2d`) never moved. `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` compares whatever `head.ref` the PR object holds against ever-moving `main` and reports its cached-feeling verdict without ever surfacing the ref name itself in the default view — so the tool kept answering truthfully about the WRONG branch, and nothing in the normal `gh pr view` output flags a branch-name mismatch; it reads exactly like "your merge attempt failed again." Diagnostic breakthrough: dropping to the raw REST object — `gh api repos/Balizero1987/Teman2/pulls/2961 --jq '{head_sha:.head.sha, ref:.head.ref, mergeable, mergeable_state}'` — immediately exposed `ref: "agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines"`, i.e. NOT the branch being pushed to. Fixed: confirmed the real PR branch was a strict ancestor of the repair-branch HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines HEAD`, safe fast-forward, 0 data loss across 368 files/+22307-3845), force-pushed the correct target (`git push origin HEAD:agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines`), renamed the local branch to match, and set upstream tracking so the drift can't silently recur for the rest of the session. General antidote for the family: **when a PR shows persistently-DIRTY/CONFLICTING status that content-diffing says should be clean, don't re-run the standard fix loop a 3rd time — go straight to `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N>` and diff `head.ref` against `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`/`git remote get-url` push target before touching anything else.** Candidate for promotion into `.claude/rules/cicatrix-superscar.md` family #9 (or its own #11 if it recurs) — not added to that file this session (out of scope: PENDING-ARMS is the fast capture, superscar promotion is a deliberate curation step) | missing arming step: (1) operator/session review + promote into cicatrix-superscar.md family #9 MEMBRI if judged non-orphan; (2) consider a cheap guard — `git remote get-url origin` + local-branch-name vs any open PR's `head.ref` for that branch — surfaced by `stop_verify.py` or a pre-push hint when they diverge | owner: me (follow-up session, CAPTURE→promotion step) | proof-of-armed: `cicatrix-superscar.md` family #9 (or new #11) MEMBRI line references this discovery, or `scar query "branch mismatch"` returns a hit

- closed 2026-07-26 | the PENDING-ARMS ledger itself carried an unresolved diff3 conflict marker on main (`||||||| parent of d47b541b78`, line 490) — and it was NOT cosmetic: the marker's seven pipes are parsed as fields, so `pending_arms_report.py` read the entry above it with `owner=?` and swallowed the entry below it (the INTERACTIVE-DEFAULT ruling) outright, while the report's own `## MALFORMED` section still said `none`. A SECOND, independent stray marker (`||||||| ebfbd71019`, the ledger's own last line, no matching `<<<<<<<`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>` anywhere) was found the same day: it blanked the owner of the 'Bali disclosure is hover-only' entry directly above it (measured live before this fix: `owner=''`, `proof='ebfbd71019'`, `cls=TECH-DEBT`, `bucket=FRESH` — invisible to both `--strict` and `--strict-phantom`, proving the residue below was real and not yet closed by the first marker's removal). Both markers are now gone. Structural fix landed in `pending_arms_report.py`: (1) `parse_entry` flags an empty (genuinely blank) owner as MALFORMED rather than silently degrading to `owner=?`; (2) `extract_open_entries` refuses to absorb a conflict-marker-shaped line (`CONFLICT_MARKER_RE`, 3 shapes — `<<<<<<<`/`|||||||`/`>>>>>>>`) into the entry being built — finalizes the entry in progress first (protecting it from corruption) and surfaces the marker as its own MALFORMED entry instead of silently dropping it; (3) both `--strict` and `--strict-phantom` now exit 1 on >=1 MALFORMED entry, not just >=1 PHANTOM-OPERATOR. Cross-family review (Codex gpt-5.6-terra, same day) caught two more real gaps in the first pass and BOTH were handled properly rather than rubber-stamped: (P1) a 4-field entry omitting the owner segment entirely back-anchors the missing_step text into owner undetected — the obvious fix (raise the pipe-count floor from `< 3` to the canonical `< 5`) was DRAFTED, then REJECTED after measuring it against the real ledger: 45/225 open entries (20%) use a different, legitimate 4-field shape (artifact + owner + proof, no missing_step — mostly FIREBREAK-style) with correctly-extracted real owners, and the floor would have flagged all 45 as MALFORMED — a far worse regression than the gap it closed. Left open, deliberately, pinned by `test_known_gap_four_field_entry_missing_owner_segment_not_caught`. (P2, FIXED) `CONFLICT_MARKER_RE`'s line-anchor alone could not tell a real orphaned marker from one deliberately quoted inside a ` ``` ` fenced code block to illustrate it — `extract_open_entries` tracks fence state and exempts marker-shaped lines while fenced (still absorbed as literal content); also dropped bare `=======` from the detected shapes (valid Markdown Setext-divider syntax too, and never the shape either live marker actually took). A third bug surfaced by the review's own test corpus: `>>>>>>>` also starts with `>` and was being silently swallowed by the pre-existing blockquote branch before ever reaching the marker check — fixed by reordering the branches. SECOND review pass (same day) on the corrected diff caught a fourth, more severe bug in the fence guard's first draft: it exempted ALL structural checks while fenced (not just the marker check), so a fence that never closes would silently absorb every subsequent line — including every later real entry — until EOF, with zero MALFORMED signal (`--strict-phantom` stays green while the rest of the ledger vanishes from the parse). Narrowed to exempt ONLY the marker check while fenced: entry-start/list-item/blank/heading detection now stay active regardless of fence state, so an unclosed fence degrades safely (worst case: a genuine marker after the accidental open goes uncaught until EOF, same class of accepted trade-off as the dropped `=======` shape) instead of catastrophically. Residual documented-not-fixed gaps in the fence guard, none reproducible in the real corpus today (zero fences of any kind currently exist in this ledger): `~~~`-style fences unrecognized, a fence closes on ANY >=3-backtick run regardless of the opening run's exact length, and 4-space-indented code blocks (no backticks) are invisible to it since `strip()` removes the indentation first | owner: me (immune-forge lane, follow-up) | proof-of-armed: `pytest scripts/tests/test_pending_arms_report.py` green (68 tests, incl. `test_innocence_unclosed_fence_does_not_swallow_the_rest_of_the_ledger` and `test_real_ledger_has_zero_malformed_after_conflict_marker_cure`) — the real ledger carries zero MALFORMED entries and `--strict-phantom` exits 0; `--strict` still correctly exits 1 on pre-existing unrelated overdue tech-debt, unchanged

The headline defect above is CONFIRMED STILL TRUE; three of the supporting premises are FALSE, and the most important of them is the PROPOSED CURE.** (a) *"0 `hreflang`"* is what an empty **lowercase** grep looks like: `/visa/second-home` serves four — `hrefLang="en" | "id" | "it" | "x-default"` — because Next's metadata API emits the attribute with a **capital L**, and HTML attributes are case-insensitive so crawlers read it fine. `grep -c 'hreflang='` returns **0** on a page that has four. (b) *"no locale ROUTING, only `?lang=`"* stopped being true for this route on 2026-08-20 (#4386): `apps/mouth/src/app/visa/second-home/[locale]/page.tsx` is real path-based routing, and `/visa/second-home/it` serves genuinely Italian server-rendered body copy (3 Italian markers vs 0 on the English URL) under a self-referencing per-locale canonical. (c) **THE CURE IS FALSIFIED, and this is the finding worth keeping.** The row predicts path-based locales give a per-locale `<html lang>` *"for free via a locale segment layout"*. That routing has been live for eleven days and `<html lang>` did **not** follow: `curl` on `/visa/second-home/it` and `/id` both return `lang="en"` in the raw response today. The row's own diagnosis of the mechanism explains exactly why and contradicts its own prescription — `<html>` lives in the **root** layout, and a locale **segment** layout is nested strictly below it, so it can never reach that attribute. The natural experiment has already been run on this perimeter: locale routing is necessary but **not sufficient**, and the root layout must separately learn the locale. Anyone implementing path-based locales site-wide on the strength of the old wording would ship the routing, watch `<html lang>` stay `en`, and have no idea why. Recorded, not cured — the cure is still a design lane, it is just a different one than this row said. Also measured, and NOT a defect so nobody "fixes" it: `/visa/second-home/studio` carries no hreflang at all, correctly — it is byte-identical under `?lang=it`/`?lang=id` (md5 `a3229ed7…`, 108037 bytes ×3) and declares only a canonical, so it exists in exactly one language and must not advertise alternates it does not have. | me (future lane — needs its own design pass, not a patch; the pass must target the ROOT layout, not a locale segment) | proof-of-armed: `curl -s "<article-url>" \| grep -o '<html[^>]*lang="[a-z]*"'` returns the article's real language with JS disabled, AND the sitemap carries per-locale URLs with reciprocal `hreflang`.

- opened 2026-08-10 | **The consent that SYMBIOSIS Law 2 now leans on is DECIDED, not implemented — and the first draft said "gap CHIUSO"** | Zero ruled on 2026-08-09 that explicit client consent is collected always, by contract, as a condition of service, so cross-border PII transit stops being a gate on vendor choice. That business decision is real and binding. What is NOT real yet is the control: there is **no contractual clause drafted, no per-client evidence service, no withdrawal mechanism, and no pre-provider enforcement** — and the status of the Google Workspace DPA (the safeguard rung of the Art. 56 cascade, which `CLAUDE.md` §14 pairs with consent as an internal rule) has never been verified or recorded anywhere in this repo. `apps/backend-rag/backend/migrations/migration_091_client_consent_log.py` only declares a legacy table; no runtime service or caller consumes it, so its presence is not evidence that consent or withdrawal is armed. `cloud_vision_gate` is also not that control: it governs only cloud OCR/vision fallbacks for documents and images. Chat-text inference is processing plus transfer when the text contains PII, and the current gateway has no shared ingress check that joins data provenance to a demonstrable per-transfer Art. 56 basis. A blind reuse of the response-side PII scanner at one router would neither establish that basis nor cover direct gateway callers. The safe rule is therefore fail-closed — keep client PII local/off-cloud or abstain while the basis is not demonstrable — but the repository does not yet enforce that rule for chat, so the gap remains explicit rather than being mislabeled an accepted risk or a compliant state. The rewrite keeps Zero's decision verbatim, preserves the statutory adequacy → binding safeguard → consent hierarchy, and separates the stricter no-cleartext-output policy (Artt. 35-39 duties) from the distinct Art. 56 transfer question. Conftests are imported during collection, before any test module, so in a PARTIAL run that names that directory the hijack wins the race and every later import of the real config gets the mock. The mock sets ~30 attributes but not `COMPANY_NAME`, so any code doing `settings.COMPANY_NAME.lower()` raises `TypeError: 'in <string>' requires string as left operand, not MagicMock`. Measured today: `pytest backend/tests/services/rag/agentic/ <two unit files>` → **43 failed**; the same tests under full-tree collection (`pytest backend/tests/ -k …`, the CI shape) → **64 passed, 0 failed**, because by then the real config is already in `sys.modules` and the guard takes its no-op branch. So CI is honest and the local partial run is the liar — which is the dangerous direction: it cost this session ~20 minutes and nearly got read as a defect in the diff under test (W107, the probe that measures a disease can have it). NOT cured here on purpose: adding `COMPANY_NAME` to the mock would turn today's loud symptom into a quieter one and leave the next unset attribute to bite the same way — the defect is the hijack, not the missing key. - closed 2026-08-10 (landing session, M5→Pro→Mini, PR-1 #3938) | **Five findings from a single multi-machine PR landing, all mitigated in-session, none of them the fix the situation first suggested** | (1) **`git branch -D $(...)` issued from inside a worktree has REPO-WIDE blast radius** — branches are shared refs across all worktrees of one repo, but the worktree-isolation hook's protection model only resolves cwd/target against "is this the main checkout", so a repo-wide destructive op launched from a non-main cwd sails through unblocked even though its true scope is repo-wide, not worktree-local. Cost a cleanup command 29 stray local branches beyond the one intended; all 29 recreated at their exact original SHA (git prints the SHA on delete, nothing was gc'd) — zero data loss, but the near-miss is the finding. Cicatrix family #3 (guard judges by form/location, not true operation scope), a new instance alongside W83-W95's command-string over/under-matches. (2) **GitHub's PR mergeability computation does NOT honor custom `.gitattributes` merge drivers** (`merge=union`, the same attribute already ledgered above for the local reaper's blob-equality bug) — a PR can sit at `mergeable: CONFLICTING`/`mergeStateStatus: DIRTY` server-side, confirmed via `gh api repos/.../pulls/N` and `gh pr update-branch` refusing, while a local `git merge` on the exact same two refs resolves cleanly with both sides' content intact (verified: both union-merge hunks present, correct line counts, no duplication). GitHub's own mergeability field is itself a proxy for "will git merge this cleanly" and it lies specifically on custom-merge-driver-dependent files — cicatrix family #9 (state-schema/proxy lies), sibling to the local-reaper instance of the same underlying gitattribute. Fix: pre-merge the base into the branch locally (where the union driver resolves it), push that merge commit, GitHub's mergeable flips clean on the new head. (3) **`ssh host 'zsh -c "..."'` (non-login shell) strips PATH** to a minimal set missing `/opt/homebrew/bin`, causing `shutil.which()`-style tool lookups to fail in ways that read exactly like a real environment gap on the remote machine. Confirmed by direct reproduction: `which npm` fails under the exact non-login invocation pattern, succeeds under `zsh -l -c`/`zsh -lc` (login shell, sources rc files). W108-class ("the probe measured its own poverty") — a diagnostic tool's own environment defect masquerading as evidence about the thing being measured. Rule going forward: every remote invocation uses a login shell. (4) **The ReDoS timing-bound test family is load-fragile** — `backend/tests/unit/core/legal/test_redos_anchor_patterns.py::TestPayloadSweep::test_no_cured_pattern_is_superlinear_on_any_swept_payload` and siblings assert a wall-clock ratio (2x input should not exceed 3x time); measured 3.1x-4.8x across M5 (×2 occurrences) and Pro (×1, 5 variants) under concurrent full-backend-suite CPU contention this session, always green on solo-run and on the quiet GitHub Actions merge-queue runner (confirmed both on the PR-branch check run and the merge-queue's own re-verification pass). NOT touched — no bound widened, no test skipped. (5) **Auto-merge arming does not survive a mergeable-state transition through CONFLICTING** — GitHub silently clears an armed `autoMergeRequest` when a PR becomes unmergeable and does NOT restore it once mergeable again; `autoMergeRequest: null` with `isInMergeQueue: false` (not the documented "queue consumed it" case, which requires `isInMergeQueue: true`) is the tell. Caught by re-checking via GraphQL after resolving (2) above and re-arming with a second `gh pr merge --auto` call. This is not a bug in any one organ: it is the ABSENCE of a shared identity for "job X is failing", and the ladder is keyed on the string, so four strings mean four independent streaks that each climb from rung 1. Context that makes it the right next target rather than the loudest one: total volume has already fallen from **~165 sends/day (08-01..08-06) to 64 / 69 / 38 / 37** as `DEATH_FLOOR_H` landed on 08-07 and today's cures removed the two biggest chronic failures — so the remaining gap to the mandate's "a few per day" is now mostly THIS multiplier, not unattended failures. **Deliberately NOT shipped in this session**, and the reason is a real design tension, not fatigue: `dlq-terminal` ("gave up, manual intervention required") is arguably a MORE severe condition than `cron-fail` and one you want to hear even having heard the first — so naive collapsing would hide an escalation, which is the W116 failure mode one level up. A family keyed on the job NAME is a per-producer key wearing a different hat: it lumps `dlq-terminal` (gave up) into the same bucket as `cron-fail` (failing). - opened 2026-08-19 (PR #4355/#4358 CI investigation, sessione M5) | **`.github/workflows/immune-enforcement.yml`'s `antidotes` job derives its path-filter from `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`/`.head.sha` (lines 50-51), which do not exist on a `merge_group` event — both come back empty, the sentinel falls into its `[ -z "$BASE_SHA" ] || [ -z "$HEAD_SHA" ]` branch (line 53), and every merge-queue entry for every PR runs the FULL battery (including the live `apt-get` inside `scripts/ci/apt_install.sh`) regardless of what it actually changed** | Confirmed two ways, not from a peer's claim alone: read the file directly (lines 47-58) — the branch is explicitly commented `# workflow_dispatch or missing event context: run the full battery`, i.e. written for `workflow_dispatch`/generic-missing-context, and `merge_group` silently falls through it because GitHub's `merge_group` event exposes `github.event.merge_group.base_sha`/`head_sha` instead, never `pull_request.*`. Independently spot-checked with `gh run list --workflow=immune-enforcement.yml --event=merge_group --limit 30`: 25 success / 5 failure, low-rate and NOT diff-correlated — PR #4351 shows both a success run and a failure run at different queue attempts, same content, different outcome. This is the same shared-mirror-stall pattern as the PENDING-ARMS row two above (organ-conformance / E2E-Playwright installer flakes), but with a distinct ROOT mechanism: those hit apt because their own steps call it; this hits apt on every queue entry, for PRs that never touch anything apt-relevant, because the sentinel can't see PR context on `merge_group` at all. Three consequences follow, none of them theoretical: (1) writing a `Reference:` line is a governance act nobody signed up to perform — `_W_NUMBER` counts every mention across the whole ledger, not just a scar's own title; (2) the promotion lands on scars OTHER than the one being written, so whoever causes it doesn't see it happen, and whoever is promoted doesn't know why; (3) a lesson can be promoted by being CITED, which is categorically easier than the failure it names actually recurring three times. **SIXTH MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-30 (infra-ghost-seat lane) — REOPENED, not another data point in either direction. General form first, because it is the actual lesson: when the mechanism is contested, doctrine prescribes the action that is safe under every surviving hypothesis; it does not encode the mechanism you have not settled. Every wrong version of this row tonight — the original claim, and both corrections drafted after it — failed by encoding a mechanism.** The FIFTH MEASUREMENT's biconditional does not survive retest. Its PROVEN half stands: `mergeQueueEntry` present still implies the scalar reads null, with no counter-example anywhere in tonight's data. Its REVERSE half — `mergeQueueEntry` absent implies the scalar reads SET — is now falsified. **Two readings, same state signature, opposite field, both first-hand this session, both querying `mergeQueueEntry` explicitly:**
- **#5236**: `mergeable: MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`, `mergeQueueEntry: null`, `autoMergeRequest.enabledAt` **SET**. History: first pass — armed once, never previously queued or ejected.
- **#5232**: same signature — `mergeable: MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`, `mergeQueueEntry: null` — `autoMergeRequest` **NULL**, confirmed settled (waited out a transient `UNKNOWN` recompute after push, re-read only once `mergeStateStatus` left `UNKNOWN`). History: armed 10:00:43Z → entered the queue → `UNMERGEABLE` at position 6 → silently ejected (the PENDING-ARMS.md union-collision pattern this same row's FOURTH MEASUREMENT already documents) → re-armed 10:27:50Z, confirmed SET at that moment → a separate merged PR (#5241) touched the same file, driving a fresh genuine CONFLICTING/DIRTY → resolved by LOCAL `git merge origin/main` (never `gh pr update-branch`), LOST=0 and RESURRECTED=0 verified with the two-sided predicate `deleted_either = (base−main) ∪ (base−branch)` (both sides empty) → the null-while-BLOCKED read above, taken with **no re-arm performed since 10:27:50Z**. Only after this read, and after reporting it, was #5232 re-armed a third time (`enabledAt: 2026-08-30T01:00:44Z`) — that third arm came AFTER both the conflict-causing event and the null read, so it explains neither; recorded here so the sequence cannot be misread later as "the re-arm is why it went null."

**The clean mechanism this would suggest — "the queue consumes the arm on entry, and ejection does not restore it, so only an explicit re-arm brings it back" — does not survive #5232's own timeline.** The 10:27:50Z re-arm came AFTER the ejection and BEFORE the second conflict; nothing in that window should have consumed it, yet the field read null regardless. The PR's own `AutoMergeEnabledEvent`/`AutoMergeDisabledEvent` timeline shows only three enables (10:00:43Z, 10:27:50Z, 01:00:44Z) and **zero disables** across the whole episode — so even the sharper timeline instrument the FOURTH MEASUREMENT relied on gives no positive evidence of a disarm here. **The mechanism is unknown. Naming one now, on this single contested case, is exactly how the original over-generalised claim (#4516, corrected at the top of this row) was born.** Do not restate it as a rule in either direction.

**Consequence for the FOURTH MEASUREMENT's local-merge tally**: it read "five PRs, six transits, zero disarms" on the strength of the timeline instrument alone. #5232 does not add a seventh disarm to that tally — the timeline still shows none — but it does add the first case where the SCALAR and the TIMELINE disagree after a local-merge resolution, which the tally's own framing did not anticipate. The tally is not overturned; it is no longer clean.

**The one guidance safe under every surviving hypothesis, and the only thing this measurement adds as doctrine**: `autoMergeRequest` NULL proves neither armed nor disarmed. Read `mergeQueueEntry` alongside it. After any conflict or ejection, re-arm regardless of what the scalar says — `gh pr merge --auto` on an already-armed PR is idempotent, measured three times over tonight (#5220 withheld intentionally and stayed armed; #5232 re-armed twice on top of a live arm with no ill effect). That is the entire correct action, and it does not require knowing which hypothesis is true.

**Arming step, updated**: unchanged in substance — the SERVER-SIDE resolution half (`gh pr update-branch`) is still the one experiment nobody has run with both instruments. Added: whoever runs it should also capture the FULL history of the test PR (was it ever queued and ejected before this test, like #5232, or is it a clean first pass, like #5236/#5227) — tonight's contradiction suggests history may matter as much as resolution method, and no experiment so far has controlled for it.

**SEVENTH MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-30 — SOLVED, not reopened, and the decisive read arrived by accident.** The lead was re-arming #5275 for ordinary reasons; `gh pr merge --auto` refused: `! Pull request Bali-Zero/Teman2#5275 is already queued to merge`, exit 0. That refusal is what exposed the true state, so a single GraphQL response was pulled to check it directly:

```
{"number":5275, "state":"OPEN", "mergeable":"MERGEABLE",
 "autoMergeRequest": null,
 "mergeQueueEntry": {"state":"QUEUED","position":3,
                     "enqueuedAt":"2026-08-30T01:17:43Z",
                     "enqueuer":{"login":"Balizero1987"}}}
```

**`autoMergeRequest` is null while the PR sits in the merge queue, actively pending — same response, same instant, no inference.** A reader of the scalar alone would have concluded this PR was unarmed and re-armed it, against a PR already queued. The decisive measurement was an error message nobody was reading as data — worth stating plainly, since the investigation had spent a day watching the wrong event types for exactly this reason. `gh pr merge --auto`'s refusal is a third independent instrument, worth naming on its own: **the CLI knows the true state and will tell you, while the API field it is built on does not.**

**The mechanism, corrected once more before shipping (the first formulation, "queue consumes on entry, ejection doesn't restore it," was still wrong — it makes ejection load-bearing when it never was):** **queue MEMBERSHIP nulls the arm — not ejection.** #5232 (now MERGED) was observed reading NULL while `AWAITING_CHECKS` at position 2, alive in the queue, not ejected on that pass at all — membership alone is sufficient, with nothing else required. The field stays null after the PR leaves the queue by any route; only an explicit fresh arm restores it, and GitHub never does so on its own; a conflict alone never touches it. **This is not permanent, and that matters as much as the null itself**: #5232 carries three separate `AutoMergeEnabledEvent`s across its life, each followed by a fresh re-entry into the queue — re-arming genuinely works, which is why the action-form guidance below was always correct regardless of which mechanism explained it.

**The sample that actually discriminates is THREE readings, not nine — say so plainly, because inflating a sample is how the row's original false doctrine got its authority in the first place.** Of the PRs cited across this row's whole history, most are now MERGED, where a null `autoMergeRequest` is trivially true (a closed PR has no pending auto-merge) and proves nothing about the mechanism. The load-bearing readings are the three still-OPEN PRs, read live: **#5275** (queued, `AWAITING_CHECKS` — **NULL**) against **#5233** (genuinely CONFLICTING, resolved by local merge, pushed, an explicit re-arm confirmed as a no-op — never entered the merge queue at any point — **SET**, `enabledAt` unchanged throughout) and **#5227** (never queued, `enabledAt` unchanged since its very first read this session — **SET**). Everything else — #5207, #5213, #5220, #5232, #5236, all now MERGED — is corroboration, not proof: their event CHAINS (where captured, e.g. #5232's full arm→queue→eject→arm→queue→eject sequence with `reason: merge_conflict` on both ejections and zero `AutoMergeDisabledEvent` anywhere) remain valid historical evidence of the transition mechanics, but their current scalar state no longer discriminates anything.

**One finding that cuts against the rule just stated, included rather than smoothed over: the event log is not complete either.** #5275 entered the queue at 01:17:43Z with **no `AutoMergeEnabledEvent` anywhere between the lead's explicit disarm at 01:10:10Z and that enqueue** — something re-armed it, and the timeline shows no trace of it. Three hypotheses, deliberately left unseparated: another lane acting under the same shared `Balizero1987` credential (the timeline's `actor` field cannot distinguish sessions, so this is structurally untraceable on this fleet as currently instrumented); an automatic queue re-entry that emits no event of its own; or an event type nobody queried tonight — which is exactly the shape of the mistake that cost a day on this row already. **"Prefer the event log to the rendered scalar" survives this pass as the better instrument, but not as a complete one: an absence in the timeline does not prove the transition did not happen.** The two instruments that have not lied once tonight, across every case measured, are `mergeQueueEntry` being present, and the CLI's own `already queued to merge` refusal.

**Why the original claim — "an armed PR that goes CONFLICTING gets disarmed, re-arm it" — survived years of use despite a wrong stated mechanism.** In this repo's actual collision pattern (the `PENDING-ARMS.md` union-driver collision this row itself documents extensively), an armed PR going CONFLICTING is overwhelmingly a PR that had also been queued at some point — so the prescribed action (re-arm) worked essentially every time. The claimed REASON — that the conflict itself disarms — was never true; queue membership disarms, and a conflict is only what commonly precedes or triggers that membership changing. The action survived because it happened to be the right response to the real mechanism too, not because the stated reason was correct.

**The instrument problem, stated plainly**: everyone measuring this tonight, including the session that wrote the FOURTH and FIFTH MEASUREMENTS above and the lead orchestrating the investigation, watched `AutoMergeEnabledEvent`/`AutoMergeDisabledEvent` only — and no disable ever fires, because no disable ever happens on this path. The real story was in `mergeQueueEntry` and `AddedToMergeQueueEvent`/`RemovedFromMergeQueueEvent` the entire time (with the caveat above: even that pair has now been shown to miss at least one transition). "Zero disarms observed" (the FOURTH MEASUREMENT's own phrase, repeated in the SIXTH) was true and uninformative for one exact reason: the events being queried could not express the thing that was happening.

**My own "never re-queued since 10:27:50Z" claim (in the now-superseded SIXTH MEASUREMENT above) was not a wrong reading — it was an unasked question, reported as an observation.** I queried `AUTO_MERGE_ENABLED_EVENT`/`AUTO_MERGE_DISABLED_EVENT` only, saw no disable event, and concluded nothing else had happened to the PR in that window. I never asked whether it had been queued again. It had — at 10:36:25Z, nine minutes after the re-arm the claim was about.

**A second, separate correction, owned by the lead and recorded here because it is the honest record of how a claim became doctrine, not to assign blame:** #5220 does not belong in this row's earlier "clean survival, re-arm withheld" framing. Fresh timeline query: #5220 has **2** `AutoMergeEnabledEvent` (09:12:23Z, 09:48:46Z), not the 1 originally claimed — a second arm was issued, the "withheld" case does not exist. The lead's own account: that claim was relayed into two other lanes and their own notes as *prova decisiva* without ever being re-derived, because it arrived with timestamps and field names and read as measured — "a measurement reported by another agent is a claim until someone re-derives it, and the ones that arrive with timestamps are the most dangerous, because they carry the appearance of the very check they skipped." One thing worth naming only as unexplored, not asserted: #5220's second arm (09:48:46Z) lands one second before #5213's third arm (09:48:47Z), consistent with (not proof of) a single batch action re-arming several PRs at once — which would mean the "withheld" claim was honest at the moment it was written and stale by the time it was published. No evidence either way exists for that; it is named and left there. This correction was found while re-deriving evidence in preparation to CITE #5220 in this row, not while auditing it — the cheapest possible placement of the check, and it caught a claim three lanes and the lead had already built on.

**Falsifier, stated so this claim can be killed cleanly if it is wrong**: this breaks if any PR ever reads SET while genuinely inside the merge queue (any `mergeQueueEntry.state` other than absent), or if any PR that has never once entered the merge queue is read NULL. Neither exists anywhere in tonight's measurements — three live discriminating cases, zero exceptions, plus the historical event chains as corroboration.

**Provenance, confirmed on every load-bearing read this pass**: the #5275 read above and the decisive #5232 chain reads were each single GraphQL responses — `mergeQueueEntry` and `autoMergeRequest` in the same query, not two calls seconds apart on a system that changes state within a second (the exact confound that produced one false contradiction earlier tonight).

**The hypothesis-safe guidance from the SIXTH MEASUREMENT is unchanged and now EXPLAINED rather than superseded — it was never wrong, only under-justified**: `autoMergeRequest` NULL proves neither armed nor disarmed by itself; read `mergeQueueEntry`, and where possible the full timeline including `AddedToMergeQueueEvent`/`RemovedFromMergeQueueEvent` (with the caveat above — even that can miss a transition); after any conflict or ejection, re-arm regardless of what the scalar says — it is idempotent, measured multiple times tonight with no ill effect, and `gh pr merge --auto`'s own refusal message is a fourth, cheap, reliable way to check before doing so. That guidance now has its mechanism: re-arming after a conflict is correct because a conflict in this repo's actual failure mode is overwhelmingly correlated with queue membership, and it is membership — not the conflict itself — that consumes the arm.

**Not touched here, deliberately**: `.claude/rules/cicatrix-superscar.md`'s scar family #9 PR-1-landing one-liner stays in its current action form ("re-arm via GraphQL after a CONFLICTING transit") — a session reading it at boot needs the correct ACTION, not the mechanism, and the file's 14-byte budget settles the question anyway. The mechanism lives here, where there is room for the chain. `cicatrix-scars.md:1279`'s GOTCHA (b) is, with this mechanism now confirmed, not actually stale in its own right (`queue:false+auto:null` = truly disarmed is now known-correct); routing any reconciliation with the L06 spec's separate transient-window finding stays with the lane the lead already assigned it to, not here.

(b) give the lint a documented, non-tripping way to reference itself — e.g. an inline `# tcc-desktop-paths: literal-ok` escape comment recognized by the scanner and excluded from the match on that line, so ADR/docstring prose can name the banned path without either tripping the guard or resorting to awkward word-splitting that erodes over time. | owner: me | proof: (a) the new guilt fixture fails today (`lint_tcc_desktop_paths.py` reports clean against it) and passes after the AST-walk lands; the lint's own test file gains both fixtures and stays green. Three spellings tested against `Draft202012Validator(content_object.schema.json)` and `ContentObject.model_validate()` off the `valid_minimal_revision_one` fixture, each case's `object_hash` freshly recomputed via `research_os.hashing.object_hash()` so no case is confounded by an unrelated hash mismatch: **key absent** → schema ACCEPT / model ACCEPT (agree); **key present with a real ref value** → schema REJECT / model REJECT (agree — both correctly refuse revision=1 superseding something); **key present as explicit `null`** → schema **REJECT** (`"...should not be valid under {'required': ['supersedes_content_object_ref']}"`) / model **ACCEPT** — diverges. Root cause on each side, both confirmed by reading the code: the schema's `allOf`/`if`-`then` (`content_object.schema.json:463,474-475`, added in `cf34c8ad7`) uses `not: {required: [...]}` for revision=1, and JSON Schema `required` tests key *presence* only, regardless of value; the model's check (`content_object.py:257`, `if self.revision == 1 and self.supersedes_content_object_ref is not None:`) tests the deserialized *value*, and a JSON `null` deserializes to Python `None`, so `is not None` is False and the check never fires. **This is not a coin-flip between two plausible readings — `hashing.py:3-5`'s own module docstring states the wire contract's rule verbatim: "`research-os/v1.0.0` uses presence-preserving null semantics (option b): an absent Pydantic field is omitted, while a field explicitly set to `None` is serialized as JSON `null`."** Absent and explicit-null are DIFFERENT documents by the contract's own stated design (different canonical bytes, different `object_hash`), and the schema's presence-based test follows that documented rule correctly; the model's `is not None` check collapses the distinction the contract says must be preserved, treating an explicit `null` as if it were absent — so at revision 1 the model wrongly ACCEPTS a document the contract, by its own stated rule, says is invalid. The open question is therefore not "which side is stricter" but which of two remedies to apply: fix the model to respect presence (not just value), or formally amend `hashing.py`'s documented rule to say revision-1 null-vs-absent should NOT be distinguished for this field — either is a legitimate ruling, but leaving the model silently contradicting its own package's documented semantics is not. Same *class* as the already-ledgered `_UTC_OFFSET_PATTERN` row above (unanchored regex — schema laxer than the model on UTC timestamp spelling) but the opposite direction: there the schema is looser than the model, here it is stricter, and here the stricter side is the one following the documented contract; cross-reference, do not conflate the two. EOF)"` message contained inline-code backticks around real shell syntax (`` `psql ...` ``, `` `TRUNCATE TABLE public.research_os_objects` ``, etc.) — bash treats backticks inside an unquoted heredoc as live command substitution, so it actually invoked `psql`, `sqlite3`, and `truncate` as real processes. Neither HOME copy imports the repo core (`grep '^import\|^from'` on both — no cross-reference); each is an independent hand-vendored duplicate. **Verified today's actual agreement, not assumed**: extracted and compared the four named pattern sets (`BLOCK_PATTERNS`, `MCP_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS`+`MCP_DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERN`, `PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS`, `SQL_DESTRUCTIVE_IN_CONTENT`) across all three files. **Correction to how this should be stated**: they are *content*-identical (same regex sources / same reason strings / same set members) across all three, but NOT literally byte-identical as raw source text — `BLOCK_PATTERNS`, `MCP_DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERN`, and `SQL_DESTRUCTIVE_IN_CONTENT` ARE byte-identical (modulo the core's extra type annotation, e.g. `: list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], str]]`); `MCP_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS` and `PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS` hold the identical values in all three but are wrapped across different line breaks (one-entry-per-line in core vs. multiple-per-line in the HOME copies) — parsed and compared as Python literals (`eval()`'d, not diffed as text) to confirm true value-equality despite the formatting difference. (3) The CI wiring that runs it, `.github/workflows/hook-innocence-gate.yml:113`, invokes `python3 scripts/guardrails_sync_check.py --hook /nonexistent/hook.py` — reproduced locally: exits 0 printing `NO LIVE HOOK at /nonexistent/hook.py — core has 21 patterns, nothing to compare. - opened 2026-08-26 (kb-current-live campaign, incidental find while dry-running the kb probe) | **Pro's `apps/backend-rag/.venv` carries `google-genai` 1.75.0 while both `requirements.lock.txt` and `requirements-prod.lock.txt` pin 2.18.1 — every local test result touching the Gemini SDK is about a version CI and production do not run** | Found because a cross-family refuter attacked an SDK-shape tripwire with exactly the right objection: an assertion that reads the INSTALLED library goes quiet on a drifted machine, i.e. it silences itself precisely where it was needed. That the contract happens to be identical in 1.75.0 and 2.18.1 (`iscoroutinefunction` True, `isasyncgenfunction` False on both) was established by installing 2.18.1 into a throwaway venv to check — it was luck, not a property anyone had verified. A major-version gap between a dev venv and the lockfile is not only a Gemini problem: it silently applies to every other pinned dependency in that venv, and nothing in this repo compares them. Armed in-repo as `test_the_installed_sdk_matches_the_version_the_lockfile_pins` (PR #5004), which is GREEN in CI (installs the lockfile) and RED on Pro until the venv is rebuilt — deliberately, with the cure named in the failure message. | owner: session (rebuild `apps/backend-rag/.venv` from `requirements.lock.txt`; a 1.75→2.18 major bump can move more than google-genai, so re-run the full backend suite after, do not reinstall a single package to make one test go green) | proof-of-armed: `apps/backend-rag/.venv/bin/python3 -c "import google.genai as g; print(g.__version__)"` prints the version `requirements.lock.txt` pins, AND `PYTHONPATH=. pytest backend/tests/unit/llm/ backend/tests/services/llm_clients/` is green with ZERO deliberate reds — never asserted from a single package's version alone **AMENDED 2026-08-26 — the named google-genai drift is CLOSED; the row's own prescribed cure turns out to be DANGEROUS as written, and one sentence of the original row was WRONG.** (1) **Closed, narrowly and provably:** `google-genai` is now 2.18.1 and `google-auth` 2.56.3, both == `requirements.lock.txt`. Only TWO packages moved, both FORWARD, no downgrades. Verified after: import chain OK, `backend/tests/unit/llm/` + `backend/tests/services/llm_clients/` **443 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed**, `backend/tests/services/rag/` **1702 passed / 12 skipped / 0 failed**, and both SDK-importing modules (`genai_client`, `gemini_service`) import clean. (2) **The cure this row prescribed — 'rebuild the venv from requirements.lock.txt' — must NOT be run as written.** Measured with `uv pip install --dry-run -r requirements.lock.txt`: **126 packages replaced, 131 installed, 11 DOWNGRADES**, against a venv that is not a dev sandbox but LIVE INFRASTRUCTURE — **7 LaunchAgents, all 7 currently loaded in launchd** (drive-intake-drain, federation-alert-dispatcher, organism.control-panel, pg-organism-bridge, verify-the-verifiers, wa-mirror-intake-sweeper, wa-mirror-session-janitor) plus 11 repo wrappers. The downgrade that actually matters, verified rather than assumed: **`presidio-analyzer` and `presidio-anonymizer` 2.2.364 → 2.2.362** — that is the PII scrubber, imported by `backend/middleware/pii_scanner.py` and `backend/app/setup/middleware_config.py`, i.e. UU PDP surface. Also `rpds-py 2026.6.3 → 0.30.0`. (3) **CORRECTION to this session's own first framing, recorded because it would have been acted on:** the `websockets 16.0 → 15.0.1` downgrade was called out as endangering the WhatsApp mirror. It does not, as stated — `grep` for websockets imports across `apps/backend-rag/backend/` and `scripts/` returns **zero**; it is a transitive dependency, not a direct one. Do not repeat that claim. (4) **Trap worth carrying forward:** `uv pip install "google-genai==2.18.1"` resolved `google-auth` to **2.57.0**, ABOVE the lockfile's 2.56.3 — installing one lock-pinned package silently introduced a NEW drift in its dependency. It had to be pinned back explicitly. Check the dependencies too, not just the package you named. (5) **Still OPEN, and this is what the row now tracks:** 423 packages installed against 273 pinned — 150 extras a `uv pip sync` would DELETE out from under those 7 live jobs — plus 126 version mismatches. Closing it is a staged operation with the daemons in mind, not a one-line reinstall, and the presidio pair should be decided deliberately rather than downgraded by a bulk command.**

- opened 2026-08-26 (PR #5004, cross-family refuter's strongest objection, left OPEN on purpose rather than argued away) | **Repairing the Gemini streaming path is operationally a LAUNCH, not a repair: since the TypeError fired on every call, the true streaming path has never served a single production request** | ⚠️ FALSE, see AMENDED at the end of this row: there is no working fallback — `nuzantara-rag` has no OpenRouter secret, so the call raises `ValueError("OpenRouter API key not configured")` rather than being served. ORIGINAL CLAIM, kept for the record: 100% of streaming traffic has been going through the caller's `"LLM stream failed"` fallback. Merging #5004 flips all of it to a path with no production history: a different latency profile, mid-stream disconnect and partial-failure modes that have never been exercised, and real `APIError`/`httpx` exceptions reaching callers where only a uniform `TypeError` ever appeared — so any alerting, metric or retry keyed to the old failure signature sees a regime change, not a fix. The fix itself is not in doubt (proven by mutation, verified on both SDK versions); what is undone is that it ships with no flag, no staged rollout and no canary named in the diff. Deliberately NOT solved by adding a flag: preserving a permanently-raising code path as the default would be preserving the defect. Solved instead by PROVING it live, per CLAUDE.md §11's post-deploy QA and the consumer-map rule — WhatsApp is the consumer that matters, since it is still on Gemini until the ChatGPT subscription is armed. | owner: session (post-merge, after the Fly deploy of #5004) | proof-of-armed: a real WhatsApp exchange through the Gemini streaming path answers correctly end-to-end, AND `"LLM stream failed"` stops appearing in `nuzantara-rag` logs for the streaming endpoint, AND a KB probe re-run no longer prints `Gemini query expansion failed` — all three, because the first alone does not distinguish streaming from the fallback that has been serving it all along ⚠️ **AMENDED 2026-08-26, three of this row's own claims measured FALSE — the row stays OPEN.** **(1) The proof-of-armed above is UNFALSIFIABLE and is replaced.** "`LLM stream failed` stops appearing" cannot distinguish a cure from an unexercised path: 75s of `nuzantara-rag` logs captured BEFORE the deploy, with the defect fully live, contained ZERO Gemini lines of any kind. Absence was already true. The falsifiable signal is the PRESENCE of an `LLM stream` SUCCESS line (the one at genai_client.py:954 that logs `chunks`), on a request whose window is known to cover it. **(2) "100% of streaming traffic has been going through the caller's `LLM stream failed` fallback" is wrong: there IS no working fallback.** `nuzantara-rag` carries no OpenRouter secret, and `_get_openrouter_client()` returns a TRUTHY client anyway (it returns None only on ImportError), so the `RuntimeError("OpenRouter fallback not available")` branch never fires — the call reaches `complete_stream`, which raises `ValueError("OpenRouter API key not configured")`. The traffic did not traverse a fallback; it raised out of `GeminiService` and whatever sat above degraded on its own. **(3) The blast radius named here is too wide.** `GeminiService.generate_response` is non-streaming in NAME only (its own comment says "Delegates to streaming path"), so every GeminiService call did hit the broken line — but there are exactly TWO doors to GeminiService, and the web chat endpoint is not one of them: `services/search/query_expander.py:72` (reachable ONLY via the non-hybrid `SearchService.search()`, since `hybrid_search` contains zero expansion calls) and `llm/providers/gemini.py` → `GeminiProvider` (the registry's `"gemini"` provider, i.e. the WhatsApp chain). `ENABLE_HYBRID_SEARCH` is set as a Fly secret, so door one is plausibly closed in production — DECLARED UNKNOWN, not asserted: the value was deliberately not read. **PROVE-LIVE ATTEMPTED TWICE, BOTH NOT PROVEN — the deploy is confirmed, the exercise is not.** Fly is on v4257 and the deployed commit contains `await self._client.aio.models.generate_content_stream(` (verified by content, not by PR state). Attempt 1, ACTIVE: a POST to `/api/blog/ask` returned 200 with a real answer, but 1679 log lines carried 0 `LLM stream` — that route goes to `hybrid_search_with_reranking` (no expansion) and synthesises through `llm_gateway.py`'s NON-streaming `generate_content`, so it never touches the fixed line; the 9 `gemini` lines came from there. Attempt 2, PASSIVE (nothing sent anywhere): a 420s window, 1758 lines, 215 HTTP requests — 100% crawler `GET /api/news/*` plus one internal cron, 0 WhatsApp, 0 `/api/blog/ask`, 0 `gemini`. **What would close this row**, and why it is not being forced: an `LLM stream` success line from organic WhatsApp traffic in a captured window. Sending a WhatsApp message to make that happen is an outward-facing act against a real number and is NOT in this lane's remit; flipping `ENABLE_HYBRID_SEARCH` to open the expansion door is a production config change for the sake of a test. Both were declined rather than done quietly. Whether WhatsApp traffic even reaches `nuzantara-rag`'s log stream is itself now open — the 7-minute window saw none. ⚠️⚠️ **THIRD AMENDMENT, 2026-08-26, and it changes the QUESTION: a real WhatsApp exchange does NOT touch the repaired method.** The owner sent a genuine client-style question to the live bot inside a captured window and the bot answered. Measured over the full 3237-line window: `whatsapp_chat` router **6** lines, `gemini` **9**, HTTP **239** — so the message arrived and Gemini WAS called (`model=gemini-2.5-flash`). And `LLM stream` — the success line `genai_client.py` emits at the repaired call site — **0**. What `backend.llm.genai_client` actually logged in that window: 4x "GenAI client initialized" and **one** "LLM structured call". Corroborated INDEPENDENTLY by the SDK itself: google-genai emitted its AFC advisory naming the method the code had just called — `AsyncModels.generate_content`, the NON-streaming one. Two unrelated signals, same conclusion. **So the row's founding claim is wrong a SECOND way, and this is the important one.** It read "100% of streaming traffic has been going through the fallback" — already corrected above because there is no working fallback. The deeper error: there may be **no streaming traffic at all**. The defect was real and fired on every call, but on a path production does not currently walk. #5004 is therefore not the LAUNCH this row called it: nothing changes regime, because nothing was travelling. **MEASURED vs INFERRED, kept apart on purpose.** MEASURED: in THIS exchange the WhatsApp path resolved to `generate_structured`/`generate_content`, not `generate_content_stream`. INFERRED, NOT asserted: that the streaming method has no live consumer at all — one exchange is one sample, and `zantara_ai_client.py:532` and `providers/gemini.py:119` both still contain streaming call sites that some other mode may reach. **The row stays OPEN but its QUESTION changes**, because the old one is unanswerable: not "prove the streaming fix live" — no traffic exists to prove it with — but **"does `GenAIClient.generate_content_stream` have ANY live consumer, and if not, say so out loud"**. That is answerable without touching production: read every mode of `zantara_ai_client` and of the registry's `"gemini"` provider and determine which, if any, is reachable in the current configuration. Until then #5004 is correct-and-dormant, not proven-live — and calling it proven-live on the strength of a bot that answered would be exactly the confusion this row was opened to prevent. Credit where due: the exchange that settled this was sent by the owner, because the session declined to send one itself.

Worse, the loop's own success back-off makes the burn take under a second: a ~90-second Telegram outage is enough to kill a money-anomaly page PERMANENTLY.** Measured on `origin/main` this turn. `outbox_consumer.py:317` defines `count_undrained`, whose docstring says out loud it reports "the numbers a probe needs to go red" and that `exhausted` "is the one that matters: those rows will never be claimed again". `grep -rn 'count_undrained' backend --include='*.py' | grep -v /tests/` returns exactly TWO hits, both of them COMMENTS inside `outbox_handlers.py` (lines 160 and 678) promising a failure will "be visible in `count_undrained`". There is no caller: no router, no scheduler branch, no health endpoint, no cron. The organ reports the right number to nobody — superscar #2, and the exact shape of W120 (the sentinel of the family reading a key the reporter never emits), here one step earlier: the reporter is never even asked. **The burn is fast, not slow.** `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5` (`outbox_consumer.py:83`) and the scheduler sleeps `0.1 if stats.dispatched else interval` (`main_api.py:191`, `interval` default 5s from `GARUDA_OUTBOX_POLL_SECONDS`). `exclude_ids` prevents re-claiming the same row within ONE pass, not across passes — so as long as ANY other job in the queue dispatches, the loop cycles every 0.1s and the failing row is re-claimed each cycle: five attempts gone in roughly half a second. With an idle queue it is 5 x 5s = ~25s. Either way a brief provider outage — Telegram 5xx, an expired bot token, a DNS blip — exhausts the row, and `attempts >= 5` means it is never claimed again. **The design is deliberate and correct as far as it goes** (`outbox_consumer.py:37-49`): a failed handler keeps its attempt bump committed, is NOT deleted, NOT marked dispatched, NOT filtered out — precisely so a probe can see it. What is missing is the probe's caller. **Latent today** for the same reason as the rest of this lane: no order exists while `GARUDA_XENDIT_SECRET_KEY` is unset, so nothing is enqueued. The first real duplicate-charge page is also the first chance to lose one silently. ADD CONSTRAINT`** — neither ownership-guarded, which is exactly why the 2026-08-26 deploy aborted with five migrations failed (`281 must be owner of table visa_decision_retention_policies`, `285 could not locate the policy_scope enum CHECK`). `backend/tests/db/test_post_d1_migrations_guard_ledger_owned_ddl.py:175-188` records how they landed anyway, verbatim: "Both were applied to production on 2026-08-26 under a temporary `GRANT visa_ledger_owner TO backend_rag_v2`, immediately revoked afterwards (the revocation was re-measured with `pg_has_role(...) = f`)", with a `GRANDFATHERED` dict naming 281 and 285. Membership is not access: the account belongs to BOTH orgs, yet a session valid on `bali-zero-7p` is worthless on `cf` without the Fly SSO hop. That, not a flaky extension, is why the browser "kept losing" the session — and it makes any `cf` automation operator-gated by construction. (b) **The org is not empty, one project inside it is**: `cf` holds a single project, `nuzantara-rag` (`4510395358904320`), whose `firstEvent` is **null** — it has never received an event, and its declared platform is `node` while the backend is Python/FastAPI. (c) Sentry's CSRF cookie is **`sentry-sc`**, passed as `X-CSRFToken` — without it a DELETE returns 403 `CSRF token missing`; the name is readable from `window.__initialData.csrfCookieName`. **Net**: a secret that sat 0600 on three machines for months was the key to a project that has never received a single event.

- opened 2026-08-29 (M5, infra/ghost-seat lane — the arming step from tonight's #5213/#5230/#5231/#5232 collision, deliberately written up as its own row rather than folded into any of the four; CORRECTED same session before arming, on team-lead review, before the wrong cure below ever shipped) | **`PENDING-ARMS.md` is itself an undeclared lockfile — and it generalizes an already-known, narrower trap to a strictly worse surface.** The same Agent PR Contract requires, by standing convention (every row in this file ends `owner: ...`, and the `modus` skill's SHIP+ARM stage treats a ledger row as part of shipping), that nearly every non-trivial agent PR append its own row to THIS file — making it a single shared file that an arbitrary number of simultaneously-armed PRs all touch. GitHub's merge-queue server-side rebuild does not honor `merge=union` here (scar family #9, PR-1-landing note), so two armed PRs both touching this file collide, and the deeper a PR sits in the queue behind others touching it, the more certain the collision. **Four worked examples from tonight, one collision each:** #5213 and #5230 (mine) entered the queue on their own and self-resolved without intervention; #5231 (not mine, a different lane) went `UNMERGEABLE` in-queue and was independently re-armed by its owning lane; #5232 (mine) went `UNMERGEABLE` at queue position 6, was silently ejected the moment #5213/#5230 landed ahead of it (`state: OPEN`, `mergeQueueEntry: null`, `autoMergeRequest: null` — looked unarmed and undamaged, was actually a live PR that had lost its arm), and needed the full local-merge / verify-LOST-and-RESURRECTED / push / re-arm recovery. **This is not a new failure shape — `evidence/pack.yml` is already documented as the identical fixed-path/`merge=union`-defeated mechanism (memory `MEMORY_MERGE_QUEUE_TRAPS.md`, "trappola #5"), but scoped narrower: only Gear-3 PRs write it.** `PENDING-ARMS.md` is the same shape on a worse surface — EVERY agent PR writes it, by contract, so the collision surface is the whole fleet, not one gear class. | missing arming step: **none prescribed here, deliberately.** This row's own first draft proposed extending Rule 5 to serialize every `PENDING-ARMS.md`-touching PR — team-lead caught that it is wrong before it was armed: unlike a Dependabot lockfile, which only a subset of PRs touch, EVERY agent PR touches this file by contract, so a serialize-on-arm rule would queue the entire fleet's ship pace behind one file — trading a rare merge-queue collision for a permanent throughput ceiling. **The primitive, named without prescribing its fix**: a shared append-only line set stored as one file is the wrong shape for concurrent writers under a merge-queue that rebuilds server-side and cannot honor `merge=union` on it — the union driver's own declaration is the admission that the file's true structure is a *set*, not a *sequence*, and a set stored as a sequence is exactly what a server-side rebuild cannot reconcile. A migration proposal (changing the file's shape to one a merge-queue CAN reconcile) is being drafted separately; this row's job is to name the mechanism and its severity, not design that fix. | owner: whoever owns the separately-drafted migration proposal — not this row, which is diagnostic only | proof-of-armed: the migration proposal lands (or is explicitly rejected with a stated reason) and either changes `PENDING-ARMS.md`'s shape so concurrent agent PRs stop colliding on it, or documents why the collision is an accepted cost. A rule that serializes every writer to this file does NOT close this row — that cure was proposed and retracted in this same row before arming

**The mechanism is HUNK ADJACENCY, not the tool.** I had written that `git merge-file --union`
forces the driver over the whole file while a real `git merge` invokes it only where hunks conflict.
False, measured both ways. What actually matters: **this file has NO TRAILING NEWLINE** (last byte
is `t`, not `0a`), so ANY append at EOF modifies the last LINE — putting a deletion within one or
two lines of EOF inside the same conflict region. Reproduced with a real `git merge`:

```
base:  - opened A / - opened STALE / - opened LAST        (no trailing newline)
mine:  delete STALE          theirs: append one row at EOF
merge: A / STALE / LAST / NEW / LAST      <- STALE RESURRECTED *and* LAST DUPLICATED, no marker
```

**And a trailing newline is the cure** — same scenario with `\n` at EOF: deletion survives, nothing
duplicated. That single byte would remove the whole mechanism, and it very likely explains the 21
duplicated rows too (they are the last-line-duplication half of the same merge). **It is not applied
here**: adding it modifies the last line, so it would collide once with every EOF-appending PR in
flight (a dozen today). That is a fleet-level timing call for the conductor, not a squad's to make
mid-wave — raised with the evidence rather than shipped.

- opened 2026-08-30 (M5, ledger-conflicts lane — found on PR #4778's own transit, confirmed independently by the seat that cured it) | **`check-ledger-no-silent-loss` goes blind on exactly the PRs it is meant to protect: its own `--depth=200` fetch of main means any PR whose merge-base is further back than that gets `CANNOT-VERIFY` instead of a verdict.** The workflow checks out the PR head with `fetch-depth: 0` — which reads as safe — and then runs `git fetch --no-tags --depth=200 origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main`. When the merge-base falls outside that shallow window, `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` exits 1 and the script reports `CANNOT-VERIFY` (exit 4). Measured with guilt and innocence on 2026-08-30: #4778's merge-base `65341d8869` sits **420** commits behind main's tip -> CANNOT-VERIFY; #5243 at 5 commits -> pass; #5294 at 1 commit -> no flag. The temporal proof is the decisive one: the SAME check was `success` on #4778's previous head `4d8afc7147` on 2026-08-24 (run `32690594867`) with the SAME base SHA, and is CANNOT-VERIFY today (run `33293748058`) purely because main has moved 420 commits since — **a PR that sits long enough breaks this check by AGEING, with its content unchanged**. The cause is structural, not a tuning miss: the countable-claims walker declares `COUNTABLE_SUBTREES = ("diff", "lanes")` but inspects only `str` nodes, and `files`/`insertions`/`deletions` are INTEGERS — invisible by construction. This is not specific to that PR: it holds for every Gear>=2 pack the repo will ever validate, and it is the exact shape the packs exist to prevent (a receipt honest when captured, false for the artifact shipped). NOT cured in #5424 on purpose — it changes the instrument that grades every PR, and #5424 is a PR about a cron's cadence; bundling it would be the "one PR, one concern" violation the contract names. | me (future lane — needs a guilt test: a pack whose `diff.files` is demonstrably wrong must go RED, plus an innocence test so a pack measured at a named SHA is not punished for its own successor commit) | proof-of-armed: craft a pack with `diff: {files: 1}` against a diff of known-different size, run `evidence_pack_lint.py` with the real `--numstat-file`, and require a non-zero exit naming the field.
